blockers.what: close and closeAllOf return the live, unfrozen TaskRecord, while sweep and list return frozen copies. The returned record is out of the table and out of liveTasks, so charge, setWindow and checkLanded already refuse it and mutating it changes nothing the table holds; the asymmetry only means a caller cannot rely on 'everything that leaves by a read or removal path is frozen' (apps/agent/src/tasks/tasks.ts:214-230, found by the `unit` tier)

The spec's per-task key for refs ('ref непрозрачен (HMAC номера узла ключом задачи)', spec §3) and the per-task snapshot store (for stale_cursor) have no home: Task carries neither, N-003 needs refOf(backendId, taskKey), and no packet names who creates the key or who drops both when a task leaves through close, closeAllOf or sweep. The one per-task value Task offers is id, which is the sessionId the agent knows, so an implementer reaching for it would make refs forgeable (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-27-bridge-b1.md N-011 packet (Produces/acceptance) and N-003 line 164 refOf(backendId, taskKey); apps/agent/src/tasks/tasks.ts Task, found by the `seam` tier)

Tasks.open puts the task in the table before its window exists. If AgentWindows.openWindow then fails (browser_offline, tab_gone), the agent never receives the sessionId, cannot close the task, and Tasks.list keeps showing it on SCR-24 (windowOpen false) until its ttl, up to 3600 s. No N-011 acceptance closes the task on that path (N-011 session.open handler (plan N-011 tests 23 and 31), consuming apps/agent/src/tasks/tasks.ts open and close, found by the `seam` tier)

Recording a window closed by the person or by a browser exit (N-011 test 31) needs the live handle, but get refuses an expired task with task_expired and list/sweep give copies that setWindow refuses. For an expired task not yet swept the event can be recorded only through a handle N-011 kept from open; Tasks has no lookup by windowId, and no Tasks test proves setWindow works on an expired live handle (N-011 test 31 (window event to setWindow); apps/agent/src/tasks/tasks.ts setWindow and get, found by the `seam` tier)

Ordering: list returns tasks oldest first (insertion order; tasks.test.ts 'list gives the tasks of every agent, oldest first'), while SCR-24 success says 'tasks first, newest first'. N-015's packet has no acceptance that pins the order, so a page that renders list() as is contradicts its screen record (docs/ux/screens.md:646 (SCR-24 success) and the N-015 packet, found by the `seam` tier)

Spec §2.3, SCR-24 and SCN-045 now say every call but close costs a step, refused ones too. charge refuses task_expired, no_such_task and budget_exhausted without a step. The exceptions are sound (no live task, or no step left) but the documents state a wider rule than the code (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-06-bridge-b1-design.md §2.3; docs/ux/screens.md SCR-24 note 'A task's time runs out'; docs/ux/scenarios.md SCN-045 Errors & recovery, found by the `seam` tier)

N-015's Consumes line (plan and packet) lists only 'Tasks.list (N-009)' and the graph edge says 'список активных задач', while its acceptance now needs goalShown and TaskSnapshot.expired, which includes tasks that are no longer active (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-27-bridge-b1.md N-015 Interfaces/Consumes and the wave table row D; .task-pipeline/packets/N-015.json, found by the `seam` tier)

Spec §2.3, SCN-045 and SCR-24 say every call but close costs a step, refused ones too. The code has two unstated exceptions. A call on a task whose time ran out is refused task_expired with no step charged, and a call on a task already out of steps is refused budget_exhausted with no step charged. The second follows from the budget being a ceiling. The first means the expired row's 'Шаги: X из Y' does not count the calls the journal lists after expiry. The purpose of the rule (retries cannot get around the budget) still holds, because neither state lets the agent do anything (apps/agent/src/tasks/tasks.ts:188-189 against docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-06-bridge-b1-design.md:107-108, docs/ux/scenarios.md:1001, docs/ux/screens.md:647, found by the `product` tier)

taskTimeOver, new in this node, says 'Okolos Agent закрывает её окно' / 'Okolos Agent is closing its window'. The task table can hold an expired task whose window is already closed (windowOpen starts false and setWindow can set it false while the task is open). In that state the row would claim a window is being closed beside taskWindowClosed. SCR-24 does not say which wording the expired row uses when the window is already closed. The page is N-015, and this node's API exposes windowOpen, so nothing is impossible yet (apps/agent/_locales/ru/messages.json and en/messages.json key taskTimeOver; apps/agent/src/tasks/tasks.ts:58, 151, 201-207; docs/ux/screens.md:647, found by the `product` tier)

After the timer sweeps an expired task, an agent's next call on it is refused no_such_task ('такой задачи нет'), not task_expired ('время задачи вышло'). SCR-24's refusal list will name the same cause in two ways, depending on whether the call came before or after the sweep (within a minute). No document promises task_expired after the window closes, so this is not false, but it is a user-visible wording the documents do not mention (apps/agent/src/tasks/tasks.ts:162-167, 243-251; docs/ux/screens.md:647, found by the `product` tier)
